prompt: coreutils chroot newroot identical old root directory behavior
answer:
When `NEWROOT` is identical to the existing `/`, GNU `coreutils chroot` avoids calling the `chroot` system call. This is done for consistency on systems where the operation is permitted for unprivileged users.

It still normally changes the working directory to `/`. The `--skip-chdir` option is allowed only in this case, letting the command retain its previous working directory.
